summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for episodic left-sided chest pain that had increased in frequency, raising concern for unstable angina given his history of coronary artery disease and prior CABG. Initial evaluation showed a mildly elevated troponin and unremarkable EKG and chest X-ray. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed severe native three-vessel coronary disease and diseased bypass grafts, but no lesions amenable to intervention. Management was optimized medically with increased isosorbide mononitrate, initiation of clopidogrel, and transition to metoprolol XL. During admission, he reported suprapubic discomfort from his chronic indwelling Foley catheter; it was changed due to mixed flora on urinalysis, though no antibiotic treatment was initiated as he remained afebrile. He also received neurology consultation for bilateral hand numbness and neck pain, diagnosed as carpal tunnel syndrome and cervical radiculopathy, with recommendations for wrist splints and a soft neck collar. Constipation was treated with lactulose. He was discharged home with improved symptoms, clear instructions on medication changes, and follow-up plans.
